extracted.intended_audience: applicants and patent professionals (patent attorneys/agents) preparing and filing PCT international applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory/recommended requirements for preparing and filing an international (PCT) patent application, including who to name, inventor identification, agents/powers of attorney, designation of States, priority claims and restoration procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who should be named first as applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended that the applicant who will represent all the applicants and to whom notifications are to be sent be named first, since he will be considered to be the common representative of all the applicants if no common agent or common representative is appointed and if that applicant is entitled to file an international application with the receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a common agent or common representative is indicated in Box No. IV, notices will be sent to that common agent/representative instead. See also paragraphs 11.015–11.017 for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying the inventor when applicant is inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the person in Box No. II is also the inventor, mark the checkbox 'This person is also inventor' — no repetition of the inventor's name/address in Box No. III is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inventor appears in Box No. III, mark 'applicant and inventor' if the inventor is also applicant, or 'inventor only' if not. If inventor is deceased or inventors differ by designated State, follow specified paragraphs (11.023–11.026 and 5.038).

rubrics_metrics.name: When to mark the 'inventor only' checkbox
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark 'inventor only' in the request form when the inventor is not also an applicant; the inventor's name and address must be indicated in one of the sub-boxes of Box No. III.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The name/address may be omitted only where none of the designated States requires the inventor's name at national filing; nevertheless it is recommended to include inventor details since national phases generally require them. Annex B lists national requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to indicate inventor's country of nationality/residence
rubrics_metrics.description: An indication of the country of which the inventor is a national or resident is not required unless the inventor is also the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same rules applicable to the indication of the applicant's name/address (paras 5.025 and 5.027) apply to inventors. For later changes in inventor details, see paragraphs 11.018 and 11.020.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different inventors for different designated States
rubrics_metrics.description: The PCT permits different inventors to be indicated for different designated States where national laws differ; indicate for which designated States the named person is inventor using item 1(iii) of the Supplemental Box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all inventors are the same for all designated States, no special indication in the Supplemental Box is required. See filled-in sample of the request form for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying designated States for multiple applicants (checkbox rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the bottom of Box No. II and each sub-box of Box No. III there are two checkboxes; one must be marked for the applicant in Box No. II and for each further applicant — or neither if the person is 'inventor only'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Box No. II 'all designated States' if applicant qualifies for all designated States; use 'the States indicated in the Supplemental Box' only in special cases (e.g., each of three applicants is applicant for different States). Same logic applies to sub-boxes of Box No. III. See Supplemental Box item 1(ii) and filled-in samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether representation by an agent is compulsory
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an applicant must be represented by an agent before the receiving Office, International Bureau and other International Authorities depends on the receiving Office (Annex C indicates this for each Office).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regardless of requirement, it is highly advisable to use a professional patent attorney or agent given importance of careful preparation and processing (see paragraph 1.004).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may be appointed as agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who can act as an agent before the Office which acts as receiving Office may be appointed as agent for an international application filed with that Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed with the International Bureau as receiving Office, any person with the right to practice before the national/regional Office of a Contracting State of which the applicant is resident or national may be appointed. An appointed agent entitled to represent before the receiving Office is automatically entitled to act before IB, ISA, and IPEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to appoint an agent (designation vs power of attorney)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agent may be appointed by designation in Box No. IV of the request if the international application is signed by the applicant; otherwise the appointment must be by a separate signed power of attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The indication must contain agent name/address in the manner indicated for applicants. It is recommended to include telephone, fax and/or e-mail to allow rapid receipt of notifications. Registered agent number may be indicated. Multiple applicants may appoint an agent representing all of them provided all applicants have signed either the request or a separate power. Model powers of attorney available on WIPO website. Where a general power authorizes filing internationals, a copy originally submitted to the receiving Office must accompany the international application unless waived by the receiving Office; general powers must be deposited with the receiving Office (except certain IB cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of power of attorney or copy of general power requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any receiving Office, ISA, IPEA or the IB may waive the requirement that a separate power of attorney be submitted; likewise may waive requirement for attaching a copy of a general power of attorney to request/demand/separate notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waivers (and any conditions) are published in Official Notices (PCT Gazette) and in Annexes C, D, E. A separate power of attorney or a copy of a general power must still be furnished for withdrawals even if waived for other cases. A waiver by one receiving Office applies only to that Office and not necessarily to other Authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointing new or additional agents after filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Further agents may be appointed at any time to represent the applicant either generally or specifically before ISA or IPEA; an agent appointed for general purposes may appoint sub-agents unless otherwise indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointment of a new agent is treated as revocation of any former appointment unless otherwise indicated in the appointing document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing/advisability of agent appointment when representation required
rubrics_metrics.description: If representation by an agent before the receiving Office is required, it is advisable that the agent be appointed by the time the international application is filed to ensure acceptance for processing by the receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice of the receiving Office regarding enforcing the requirement mirrors that for national/regional applications. If appointment not obligatory, it may be made at filing or later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether a person signing for a corporate applicant is an agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the person who signs the request for a corporate applicant is regarded as an agent depends on the nature of the authorization — whether signing on behalf of the corporate applicant or as appointed agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the person's name is indicated in Box No. IV and 'agent' checkbox is marked, the person is regarded as agent and power of attorney may be required. If corporate applicant indicated in Box No. IV and 'common representative' checkbox is marked, the person who signs will not be regarded as agent. Listing a person as part of the address for correspondence as common representative does not make them an agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common representative among several applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: If a common agent is not appointed by all applicants, one applicant may be appointed by the others as common representative; if neither a common agent nor common representative is appointed, the first-named applicant entitled to file is automatically considered the deemed common representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rules 2.2bis and 90.2 and paragraph 11.005–11.006 for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-mail notifications to agent/common representative
rubrics_metrics.description: If an e-mail address is indicated in Box No. IV, the receiving Office, ISA (if they provide the service) and the IB will send notifications in respect of the international application to the agent or common representative at that e-mail address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually no paper notifications will be sent if e-mail used. If no e-mail or agent chooses postal mail by checking the box, notifications will be sent exclusively by postal mail (subject to whether the Office provides e-mail service). If e-mails provided for both applicant and agent, notifications are only sent to the appointed agent/common representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special address for correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence is sent to the appointed agent or common representative; where no agent is appointed correspondence goes to the applicant or deemed common representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant wishes correspondence to be sent to a different address (not an agent/common representative), that address must be indicated in Box No. IV and the last check-box of Box No. IV must be marked (do not mark it if 'agent' or 'common representative' has been marked).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of States by filing the request (automatic designation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For international applications filed after 1 January 2004, filing the request automatically constitutes the designation of all Contracting States that are bound by the Treaty on the international filing date and indicates that the international application is for the grant of every kind of protection available by designation, with specific effects under Articles 43/44/45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies even if not using the current Form PCT/RO/101 or if the international filing date is changed to a date on/after 1 January 2004. See paragraph 5.052 for specifics (i–iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluding certain States from automatic designation
rubrics_metrics.description: As an exception, Germany, Japan and the Republic of Korea may be excluded from designation; check-boxes exist for applicants who want to avoid designating those States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These States notified IB that designation may cause earlier national application to cease to have effect if priority of an earlier national application is claimed. Annex B explains particular conditions per State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension/validation of a European patent via PCT filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A European patent granted on an international application may, if conditions are met, be extended to or validated in States having Extension/Validation Agreements with the EPO; filing the international application constitutes designation of EPO and of the States to which extension/validation may apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details on steps for national-phase entry and fees are published in the EPO Official Journal and National Chapter Summary (EP); Annex B (EP) lists applicable States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of kind of protection during international phase
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not possible during the international phase to indicate the wish to obtain a certain kind of protection for a particular designated Office; the filing indicates request for every kind of protection available by designation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of type of protection (e.g., utility model, petty patent) can only be made in the national phase before respective designated Offices. It is possible, however, to withdraw a certain type of protection for a designation. Annexes B list available kinds of protection per State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Including parent/continuation information in request
rubrics_metrics.description: Where, when entering national phase, a title of addition is sought or applicant wishes the international application to be treated as continuation/continuation-in-part, the applicant may indicate this information and the parent application/grant in the Supplemental Box following the designated State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use item 2 or 3 of the Supplemental Box for this indication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting or adding continuation/parent indications in request
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may correct or add any indication referred to in Rule 4.11 by notice to the IB within 16 months from the priority date, subject to timing relative to technical preparations for international publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If notice received after time limit but before technical preparations complete, it is considered received on last day of time limit. IB will notify applicant of corrections/additions made. If not timely, IB will inform applicant to submit indication/correction directly to designated Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis and required content of a priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Any international application may contain a declaration claiming priority of one or more earlier applications filed in Paris Convention countries or in WTO members; earlier regional or international applications may also be basis. Any priority claim must be made in the request and contain necessary indications to uniquely identify the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For national earlier applications include country, filing date and number; for regional applications indicate Office and, where necessary, at least one country party to the Paris Convention or WTO; for international earlier applications indicate the receiving Office. Two-letter country/Office codes may be used. Subject to conditions, priority claims may be corrected/added after filing (see paras 6.038–6.044).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'priority date'
rubrics_metrics.description: Where priority is claimed, 'priority date' means the filing date of the application whose priority is claimed; where none, it means the filing date of the international application. For multiple claims, it is the earliest claimed filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'priority period'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Priority period' means 12 months from the filing date of the earlier application whose priority is claimed; the day of filing of the earlier application is not included in this period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To validly claim priority, the international application must normally be filed within the priority period, otherwise the right of priority is lost, subject to limited exceptions in certain Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles governing the right of priority under PCT
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT does not change Paris Convention Article 4 provisions; priority claims under PCT are treated in line with Paris Convention and TRIPS obligations. The priority claim is important for computing PCT time limits. Validity is not determined during the international phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A priority claim will be considered not made for PCT purposes if the earlier application wasn't filed in a Paris Convention country or WTO member, if filed more than two months after expiration of priority period (subject to corrections), or if required details are missing. Corrections may be possible per specified paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to indicate dates in the priority claim and correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Each date must be indicated by day (Arabic), month name and year (Arabic) in that order, and should be repeated in parentheses with two-digit day and month and four-digit year separated by periods/slants/hyphens (e.g., '20 March 2006 (20.03.2006)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Section 110 formatting rules for all dates in the international application or correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing after the priority period but within two months (retention in international phase)
rubrics_metrics.description: If international filing date is later than the priority period expiration but within two months from that date, the priority claim will not be declared void for international phase purposes and, if it is the only or earliest priority claim, it will continue to serve as the basis to calculate PCT time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This retention does not guarantee validity in national phase. Applicant may request restoration of the right of priority with a receiving Office; some receiving Offices have declared incompatibility with restoration provisions and will not accept such requests — see WIPO list. Applicants aware of need to restore should file with an Office that accepts such requests (e.g., receiving Office of the International Bureau accepts such requests). If needed after filing, applicant may request transmission to IB RO under Rule 19.4(a)(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for requests to restore the right of priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit to comply with requirements to request restoration of the right of priority is two months from the date on which the priority period expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the receiving Office requires declarations/evidence supporting the reasons for failure to file within the priority period, it will allow a reasonable time under the circumstances to furnish those documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to file a request for restoration of the right of priority and its requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The request can be filed via the request form (Box VI) which includes an option, via ePCT, or separately by letter to the receiving Office. For success the following must be met: (a) the international application must contain a priority claim and must have been filed within two months from expiry of the priority period (or the claim added within that time); (b) the request must state reasons for failure to timely file (submitted as a separate document); (c) any applicable fee for restoration must be paid before the two-month time limit (fee payment period may be extended up to two months); (d) if required, declaration/evidence in support of reasons should be furnished with the request or upon invitation by the receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In multiple priority claims, clarify which priority claim restoration is requested for. Annex C indicates which receiving Offices require a fee and what restoration criteria they apply. See Rules 26bis.1, 26bis.3 and related paragraphs (5.062–5.064).

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving Office criteria for restoration (reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Receiving Offices apply specific restoration criteria to requests; applicants should consult Annex C and paragraph 5.065 for the criteria applied by particular Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text indicates that different Offices may apply different restoration criteria and that applicants should take these into account when choosing where to file if restoration may be needed.
